bullets: Instead of restricting the Activations of each layer to be strictly Zero mean and unit variance, Normalization allows the network to learn parameters γ and β that can convert the mean and variance to any value that Minimizes Loss.
labels: Input: Values of x over a mini-batch: 𝓑 = {x_{1...m}};
Parameters to be learned: γ, β
equations: y_i ← γ x̂_i + β ≡ BN_{γ,β}(x_i)   [LaTeX: y_i \leftarrow \gamma\,\widehat{x}_i + \beta \equiv \mathrm{BN}_{\gamma,\beta}(x_i)]

Then four display equations, each with a right-aligned sans-serif comment: (1) μ_𝓑 ← (1/m)∑_{i=1}^{m} x_i, μ_𝓑 on lavender highlight, comment '// mini-batch mean'; (2) σ²_𝓑 ← (1/m)∑_{i=1}^{m}(x_i − μ_𝓑)², σ²_𝓑 on lavender highlight, comment '// mini-batch variance'; (3) x̂_i ← (x_i − μ_𝓑)/√(σ²_𝓑 + ε), left-hand x̂_i on pink highlight, numerator 'x_i − μ_𝓑' and denominator '√(σ²_𝓑 + ε)' each on light-blue highlights, comment '// normalize' on pink highlight; (4) y_i ← γx̂_i + β ≡ BN_{γ,β}(x_i), y_i encircled by an orange ellipse outline, γ and β on green highlights, x̂_i on pink highlight, comment '// scale and shift' on orange highlight.

recreation_brief:
1. Slide setup: 16:9, background very light gray #F2F2F2 (near-white); add a solid black rectangle across the full bottom edge (~5% height) to mimic the video letterbox.
2. Title: text box centered at top (~10% from top), text 'Normalization Parameters', bold serif (Times New Roman/Georgia), ~36pt, color #C00000.
3. Slide number: draw an oval (~36px diameter) at top-right (~90% horizontal, ~13% vertical), fill #FFFF99, border 2pt #8B0000; add text '40' in bold red #C00000 ~14pt centered inside.
4. Intro box: draw a rectangle from ~9% to ~91% width, ~19% to ~35% height; white/no fill, border 2pt #C00000. Inside, serif ~16pt paragraph, wrapped as three lines, exact text: 'Instead of restricting the Activations of each layer to be strictly Zero mean and unit variance, Normalization allows the network to learn parameters γ and β that can convert the mean and variance to any value that Minimizes Loss.' Inline formatting: 'strictly' = #2222CC italic; 'Zero' and 'unit' = #2222CC bold; 'mean and' and 'variance' = #2222CC; 'learn parameters' = bold #008000 on #90EE90 highlight; 'γ' and 'β' = #008000 (β bold); 'convert the mean and variance to any value that' = #C00000 italic underlined; 'Minimizes Loss.' = #C00000 bold italic underlined.
5. Algorithm panel: white rectangle with 1.5pt black border from ~15% to ~58% width, ~38% to ~92% height; leave the right half of the lower slide empty.
6. Panel header (LaTeX-style serif, e.g. Cambria Math/STIX): line 1: bold 'Input:' then 'Values of x over a mini-batch: 𝓑 = {x_{1...m}};' with x italic and 𝓑 calligraphic; line 2 indented with the whole phrase on a #90EE90 highlight: 'Parameters to be learned: γ, β' (γ, β italic); line 3: bold 'Output:' then '{y_i = BN_{γ,β}(x_i)}'.
7. Equation 1 via equation editor (LaTeX: \mu_{\mathcal{B}} \leftarrow \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m} x_i): place a #9999CC highlight behind 'μ_𝓑'; right-aligned sans-serif comment '// mini-batch mean' in dark gray/black.
8. Equation 2 (LaTeX: \sigma_{\mathcal{B}}^2 \leftarrow \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}(x_i - \mu_{\mathcal{B}})^2): #9999CC highlight behind 'σ²_𝓑'; comment '// mini-batch variance'.
9. Equation 3 (LaTeX: \widehat{x}_i \leftarrow \frac{x_i - \mu_{\mathcal{B}}}{\sqrt{\sigma_{\mathcal{B}}^2 + \epsilon}}): #FF9C9C highlight behind left-hand 'x̂_i'; #A6D0F2 highlights behind numerator 'x_i − μ_𝓑' and denominator '√(σ²_𝓑 + ε)'; comment '// normalize' on a #FF9C9C highlight.
10. Equation 4 (LaTeX: y_i \leftarrow \gamma \widehat{x}_i + \beta \equiv \mathrm{BN}_{\gamma,\beta}(x_i)): draw an unfilled ellipse with #FF8C00 outline around 'y_i'; #90EE90 highlights behind 'γ' and 'β'; #FF9C9C highlight behind 'x̂_i'; comment '// scale and shift' on a #FFA64D highlight.
11. Set all four '// comments' in a small sans-serif font (~12pt), one per equation row, right-aligned within the panel.
